name: Jump rope
summary: Skip a rope with small, quick hops. High-intensity cardio that also trains foot and ankle springiness, using almost no space.
setup: Stand on the middle of the rope: the handles should reach your armpits. Shorten it if longer.
Hold the handles lightly at hip height, about 20 to 30 cm out from your body, elbows close to your ribs.
Jump on a forgiving surface: wood, rubber or a mat, not concrete.

steps.text: Turn the rope with small circles of your wrists. Your arms barely move.
Hop just as the rope reaches your toes. Two or three centimetres is enough to clear it.
Land softly on the balls of your feet with knees slightly bent, heels just above the floor, and go straight into the next hop.

jointCues.cue: Make the circles with the wrists, not the shoulders.
jointCues.why: Big arm circles slow the rope and tire the shoulders in seconds.

jointCues.cue: Close to your sides, bent about 90 degrees or a little more open.
jointCues.why: Elbows drifting out shortens the rope and causes trips.
Shrugging tightens the neck and makes the rope rise.

jointCues.cue: Soft knees; the spring comes from the ankles and calves.
jointCues.why: Landing stiff-legged or on the heels sends the impact up the shins and knees.

jointCues.cue: Tall, eyes forward, not looking at your feet.
jointCues.why: Looking down rounds the back and throws off the rhythm.

breathing: Breathe steadily through nose and mouth. In longer rounds, match it to the rhythm, for example in for four hops and out for four.
tempo: Beginners: 30 s on, 30 s off. Typical pace 100 to 140 turns per minute.

mistakes.fix: Hop just high enough to clear the rope.
Speed up the wrists slightly so one hop matches one turn.
Stay on the balls of your feet.

safety: Build up slowly: calves and Achilles tendons need a few weeks to adapt.

cues.text: Turn the rope with your wrists; arms barely move
Hop 2 to 3 cm, just enough to clear it
Land softly on the balls of your feet, knees soft
